learning_outcomes.text: The student acquires knowledge about individual genres of popular music - their history, specificity, and socio-cultural significance (rock, heavy metal, reggae, rap, hip-hop, dance music, disco polo).
The student is aware of the need for scientific reflection on popular music and learns basic theories related to the study of popular music and scientific methods for researching this issue.
The student becomes familiar with the history of popular music development in Poland and worldwide.

The student knows basic terminology related to the theory and research of popular music, has knowledge about the history of scientific reflection on popular music and its contemporary form, and knows the history of popular music development in Poland and worldwide.
The student has knowledge about individual forms of popular music - knows their history, specificity, and socio-cultural significance.
The student understands what distinguishes popular music from other types of music (e.g., classical, folk, etc.), and can connect popular music with its cultural context.
Ability to effectively organize project and analytical work.

syllabus_topics: Main trends of popular music: Introduction
History of reflection on popular music in the context of popular culture
Studies on popular music vs. sociology of music
Studies on fans and the phenomenon of neo-tribes
Rock of the 1960s - politics and counterculture
Rap music and hip hop culture
Disco polo - a Polish phenomenon of popular music
MTV, pop music and music videos
Contemporary dance music and club culture
assessment_rules: The condition for passing is the preparation of a written essay. Students participate in classes, learning subsequent teaching content according to the course syllabus. Students should ask questions and clarify doubts on an ongoing basis. Audiovisual recording of the lecture requires the lecturer's consent.
